name: Learn: kubeadm (upgrade, join, certs)
description: Operate a kubeadm-managed cluster step by step — inspect component versions, mint a worker join token, perform the drain/uncordon maintenance dance, renew control-plane certificates, and read an upgrade plan. The node-level lifecycle tasks the CKA leans on.
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration (25%). Goal: inspect kubeadm/kubelet versions, generate a worker join command, drain and uncordon a node for maintenance, renew expiring control-plane certificates, and read a kubeadm upgrade plan — the cluster lifecycle tasks kubeadm clusters demand on exam day.

questions.title: Inspect component versions
questions.teach:
A kubeadm cluster has distinct version surfaces: the **kubeadm** CLI, the **kubelet** on each node, and the **control-plane components** (apiserver/controller-manager/scheduler) that run as static pods. Before any upgrade you must know what you're running.

**Ways to read versions:**
- `kubeadm version` (add `-o short` for just the tag, `-o json` to parse).
- `kubelet --version` — prints `Kubernetes v...`.
- `kubectl version` — client + server (apiserver). `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows the per-node kubelet **and** container-runtime versions in the KUBELET-VERSION / CONTAINER-RUNTIME columns.
- `kubectl version` without `--short` now warns; parse `-o json`/`-o yaml` for scripts (the old `--short` flag is gone in recent releases).

**Skew-policy gotchas (why versions matter):**
- Upgrade **one minor version at a time** (1.29→1.30→1.31), never skip a minor.
- **Order:** upgrade `kubeadm` first, then the control plane, then `kubelet`/`kubectl` on each node.
- kubelet may trail the apiserver by up to **3 minor** versions (older policy was 2 — know your target release), but must **never be newer** than the apiserver.
- These binaries live on the node, not your laptop, so you reach them with `docker exec` into the node container.
questions.prompt:
On the control-plane node ($CP), capture the kubeadm and kubelet versions and write BOTH, one per line, to `/tmp/versions.txt` on $CP.

Target: `docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/versions.txt` shows a `kubeadm` line and a `Kubernetes v...` (kubelet) line.
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubeadm version; kubelet --version' > /tmp/out` won't land on the node — redirect INSIDE the node: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubeadm version -o short > /tmp/versions.txt; kubelet --version >> /tmp/versions.txt'`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubeadm version -o short > /tmp/versions.txt; kubelet --version >> /tmp/versions.txt'
docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/versions.txt

questions.title: Generate a worker join command
questions.teach:
To add a worker you need a **bootstrap token** plus the CA cert hash so the new node can authenticate to and trust the apiserver.

**Minting the join command:**
- `kubeadm token create --print-join-command` — one shot: mints a fresh token **and** prints the full `kubeadm join <api>:6443 --token ... --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:...` line.
- Already have a token? `kubeadm token list` to see them; `kubeadm token delete <id>` to revoke.
- Need just the CA hash by hand: `openssl x509 -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt -noout -pubkey | openssl rsa -pubin -outform DER | openssl dgst -sha256`.

**Token / Secret details & gotchas:**
- Each bootstrap token is a Secret named `bootstrap-token-<id>` in **`kube-system`**, type `bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token` — find them with `--field-selector type=bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token` (label/name filters won't catch them cleanly).
- Default TTL is **24h**; set `--ttl 0` for a never-expiring token or `--ttl 1h` to shorten. Expired tokens silently fail a join.
- **Joining a control-plane node** also needs a **certificate key** (upload certs first: `kubeadm init phase upload-certs --upload-certs`) plus `--control-plane --certificate-key <key>` — the plain print-join-command only covers **workers**.
- `kubeadm token create` alone (without `--print-join-command`) just prints the token string.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, generate a fresh worker join command with kubeadm so that a new bootstrap-token Secret is created in `kube-system`.

Target: at least one Secret of type `bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token` exists in `kube-system`.
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm token create --print-join-command`. Verify the Secret with `kubectl -n kube-system get secrets --field-selector type=bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm token create --print-join-command
kubectl -n kube-system get secrets --field-selector type=bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token

verification.description: a bootstrap-token Secret exists in kube-system

questions.title: Drain then uncordon a node
questions.teach:
Before upgrading a node's kubelet (or doing any maintenance) you **drain** it. The real upgrade dance is `drain → upgrade kubelet → uncordon`, **one node at a time**.

**The three verbs:**
- `kubectl cordon <node>` — only marks `.spec.unschedulable: true`; **existing pods keep running**, no new pods scheduled.
- `kubectl drain <node>` — cordons **and** evicts the node's pods (respecting PodDisruptionBudgets via the eviction API).
- `kubectl uncordon <node>` — clears `unschedulable` so the scheduler uses it again.

**drain flags & gotchas:**
- `--ignore-daemonsets` — **almost always required**; DaemonSet pods aren't drained (nothing would reschedule them), so without it drain errors out.
- `--delete-emptydir-data` — required if any pod uses an emptyDir, else drain refuses (you accept the data loss).
- `--force` — required to evict **bare/unmanaged pods** (not backed by a controller) since nothing recreates them.
- A restrictive **PodDisruptionBudget** can block/hang the eviction — a classic trap; `--disable-eviction` falls back to delete (bypasses PDBs).
- Drain only moves pods **off** the node; it does **not** cordon other nodes, and it doesn't delete the pod definitions for controller-managed workloads (they reschedule elsewhere). Remember to `uncordon` afterward — a forgotten cordon leaves capacity stranded.
questions.prompt:
A test Pod `drain-me` is pinned to worker $W2. Drain $W2 (evicting the workload), then uncordon it when "maintenance" is done.

Target: $W2 ends `schedulable` (`.spec.unschedulable` unset) AND no `drain-me` pod remains running on $W2.
questions.hint: `kubectl drain "$W2" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`, confirm the pod moved/left with `kubectl get pods -o wide`, then `kubectl uncordon "$W2"`.
questions.solution:
kubectl drain "$W2" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
kubectl get pods -o wide            # drain-me no longer on $W2
kubectl uncordon "$W2"
kubectl get node "$W2"              # Ready, not SchedulingDisabled

verification.description: $W2 is schedulable and holds no drain-me pod

questions.title: Renew control-plane certificates
questions.teach:
kubeadm issues the control-plane's client/serving certs under `/etc/kubernetes/pki/` with a **1-year** lifetime (the CA itself is **10 years**). A normal `kubeadm upgrade` renews them automatically — manual renewal is for clusters that aren't upgraded often enough.

**Checking & renewing:**
- `kubeadm certs check-expiration` — lists every cert, its expiry, and whether its CA can renew it.
- `kubeadm certs renew <name>` — renew one (e.g. `apiserver`, `apiserver-kubelet-client`, `front-proxy-client`, `admin.conf`).
- `kubeadm certs renew all` — renew every component cert at once.
- Read expiry straight from the file: `openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt`.

**Gotchas:**
- Renewal **rewrites the .crt/.key on disk but does NOT restart** the static pods — the running apiserver keeps using the old cert until it restarts. Force a reload by moving the manifests out of `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` and back (or restart kubelet); a `kubeadm upgrade apply` restarts them for you.
- Renewing the **kubeconfig** files (`admin.conf`, `controller-manager.conf`, `scheduler.conf`) also refreshes the embedded client certs — re-copy `admin.conf` to `~/.kube/config` if you use it.
- You **can't renew the CA this way** — only certs signed by an on-disk CA renew; an expired CA is a full re-issue job.
- `kubeadm certs certificate-key` generates the key for uploading certs when joining extra control-plane nodes (different concern from renewal).
questions.prompt:
On $CP, check cert expiration, then renew the apiserver certificate so its NotAfter date is pushed to roughly one year from now.

Target: `/etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt` on $CP has been **renewed** — its serial number differs from the one recorded before you started (NotAfter now pushed ~1 year out).
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs check-expiration`, then `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs renew apiserver`. Confirm with `docker exec "$CP" openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs check-expiration
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm certs renew apiserver
docker exec "$CP" openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt

questions.title: Read a kubeadm upgrade plan
questions.teach:
`kubeadm upgrade plan` inspects the cluster and prints which versions you can upgrade to, plus the component versions it would bump. It's a **read-only report** — you always run it before `kubeadm upgrade apply`.

**The upgrade workflow (what the plan precedes):**
1. Upgrade the `kubeadm` binary to the target version first (it refuses to plan an upgrade it can't perform).
2. `kubeadm upgrade plan` — review targets.
3. On the **first** control-plane node: `kubeadm upgrade apply v1.X.Y`.
4. On **additional** control-plane nodes: `kubeadm upgrade node` (not `apply`).
5. On **workers**: `kubeadm upgrade node`, then `drain → upgrade kubelet/kubectl → uncordon`.

**Gotchas:**
- `apply` targets a **specific version** (`kubeadm upgrade apply v1.30.2`) — it won't guess.
- Only the **first** control-plane node uses `apply`; everything else uses `upgrade node` — mixing these up is a common exam slip.
- The plan reasons about the **server (apiserver)** version. Confirm the control plane is healthy first: apiserver/controller-manager/scheduler static pods Running. `kubectl version` (parse `-o json`/`-o yaml`) shows that server version; the old `--short` flag is removed.
- `kubeadm upgrade apply` auto-renews control-plane certs unless you pass `--certificate-renewal=false`.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, run `kubeadm upgrade plan` and read its output. To prove the control plane is healthy and reporting a version, write the server (apiserver) version string to `/tmp/serverversion.txt` on $CP.

Target: `/tmp/serverversion.txt` on $CP contains a `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` Kubernetes version.
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm upgrade plan` to read the plan. Then capture the server version onto the node: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf version -o json | grep -o "v[0-9]*\.[0-9]*\.[0-9]*" | head -1 > /tmp/serverversion.txt'`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm upgrade plan
docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf version -o json | grep -oE "v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" | head -1 > /tmp/serverversion.txt'
docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/serverversion.txt
